title: introduce per-prompt sensitivity profiles and differential regression gate
author: Aisha Khatri
release_notes: Add per-prompt sensitivity profiling and a CI gate that fails builds when perturbation-driven differential scores exceed calibrated thresholds. Includes docs and a small migration guide for existing prompt sets.
description:
Context and motivation:
We observe intermittent production regressions that only appear for narrow prompt variants — high sensitivity to surface-form perturbations or tokenization boundaries. Existing cohort-level gates (cohort drift, ensemble probes) catch many regressions but miss prompt-level fragility. This PR introduces per-prompt sensitivity profiles and a differential regression CI hook that uses controlled perturbation ensembles to detect fragile prompts early in CI.

What this change does (high level):
- New data artifact: per-prompt sensitivity profile (stored as a compact vector of sensitivity metrics and baseline output fingerprints).
- Perturbation ensemble runner: generates controlled variants (synonym swaps, punctuation/noise, casing, small reorderings) and computes response dispersion and semantic-shift metrics against baseline.
- Differential regression gate: compares current PR run to the baseline snapshot for the prompt-set, applying per-prompt calibrated thresholds. The gate fails when a configurable fraction of prompts exceed their sensitivity tolerance.
- Admin tooling: CLI to backfill profiles, inspect per-prompt metrics, and override thresholds for known brittle prompts.
- Docs: guidance on interpreting sensitivity signals and migrating existing prompt sets.

Why this approach: a per-prompt view lets teams triage regressions to individual prompts and decide whether to tighten model quality or update prompt templates. The differential gate avoids noisy global failures by calibrating thresholds per prompt based on historical perturbation variance.

Small illustrative snippet (CI hook exit behavior):
```
# pseudo
if fraction_prompts_over_threshold > gate_tolerance:
  print("Differential sensitivity gate: FAILED - fraction=%.2f" % fraction)
  sys.exit(2)
else:
  print("Differential sensitivity gate: PASS - fraction=%.2f" % fraction)
  sys.exit(0)
```

CI run history for this PR:
- initial pipeline (2026-02-16): fail — nondeterministic perturbation seed.
- rerun after fix (2026-02-17): fail — discovered embedding model mismatch warnings surfaced as error in strict mode. Converted to warn by default.
- final run (2026-02-20): pass (all checks green).
CI checks: unit-tests, linters, integration-smoke, sensitivity-gate (pass).

Operational notes and configuration: 
- Default gate behavior: warn if less than 5% of prompt-set breached; fail if >= 5% AND median differential score per-breaching-prompt > calibrated threshold.
- Config knobs: per-prompt threshold override, gate_tolerance (fraction), smoothing_window, perturbation_strategies (list).
- Baseline snapshots are stored under s3://redwood-eval/baselines/sensitivity/YYYYMMDD/ and are rotated weekly. Backfill tool provided for historical profiling.

Migration and backward compatibility:
- Adding profiles is additive; existing prompt-sets continue to run. The CI hook is opt-in per repo via ci/pipeline.yaml flags. The CLI backfill command recommended before enabling the gate to avoid noisy initial failures.

Docs and examples:
- docs/ops/prompt-sensitivity.md explains the metrics, how to interpret per-prompt variance vs semantic-shift, and sample remediation steps (tighten prompts, add augmentations, mark prompt as brittle).
